title: Janus Infinite Faces — Post-Compromise Temporal Root Recovery Test
test_question: What happens when a root that legitimately attested Janus history becomes compromised later and can now sign forged future history?

critical_finding.statement: Once enough current signing roots are compromised, signatures alone cannot distinguish a forged post-compromise branch from a legitimate branch using the same compromised credentials.

temporal_trust_model.ROOT_EPOCH: A bounded era in which a specific root credential lineage is eligible for a specific policy.
temporal_trust_model.COMPROMISE_HORIZON: Earliest sequence/time coordinate at which a root is credibly treated as no longer trustworthy; may be uncertain and represented as an interval.
temporal_trust_model.PRE_HORIZON_ATTESTATION: Not automatically invalidated by later compromise if independently preserved and no evidence moves compromise earlier.
temporal_trust_model.POST_HORIZON_ATTESTATION: CONTESTED unless re-established through uncompromised evidence and recovery policy.

steps: freeze external commits dependent on contested roots
preserve all alternate branches as forensic objects
determine the earliest defensible compromise horizon or interval from external evidence
select the latest independently archived checkpoint strictly before the horizon that satisfied the then-valid policy
activate a separately governed recovery credential/policy
replay suffix events only from evidence not dependent solely on compromised roots
quarantine unrecoverable or equivocal suffix events
rotate operational roots into a new ROOT_EPOCH
emit a recovery checkpoint referencing the old checkpoint and compromise record

uncertainty_rule.rule: If compromise time is uncertain, widen the contested interval rather than invent a precise safe boundary.
uncertainty_rule.consequence: Some otherwise legitimate events may remain UNRESOLVED until independent evidence reattests them.

failure_ceiling.meaning: The architecture admits a real terminal trust failure rather than manufacturing PASS.
